name: Known cryptominer binary started on a server
description: Lab rule 2 of 3 for the CTIA cryptomining-001 scenario. The single most common way a SOC finds cryptomining at all: match the miner binary by name. In a real estate this rule fires constantly, because attackers rename the binary, wrap it in a loader, or run it from memory - which is exactly why a detection estate needs more than one rule. In this lab it fires once, on the child of the PowerShell that rule 1 caught. Deliberately included even though it names the mining binary, because the alert text the student was handed already says a second unfamiliar executable appeared, and because a rule that only ever fires once is the most realistic thing on the whole Alerts page. A production version of this rule would match on file hash, signer, and image path as well as name, and would be joined to rule 1 so that one download event and one miner event are triaged as a single incident rather than two.
